title: OpenAI Launches Ultrafast Mode for GPT-5.6 Sol at 750 Tokens Per Second
excerpt: Powered by Cerebras custom silicon, the new inference tier delivers 14x the standard speed for enterprise developers running agentic AI workflows.
body:
• OpenAI has launched Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, powered by Cerebras hardware, delivering up to 750 tokens per second — roughly 14 times faster than standard inference speeds.
  • The speed boost is enabled by Cerebras's Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3), which uses 44 GB of on-chip SRAM with 21 petabytes per second of memory bandwidth, eliminating traditional GPU bottlenecks.
  • Ultrafast mode is priced at $12.50 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens, targeting enterprise developers running latency-sensitive agentic workflows.

OpenAI has introduced Ultrafast, a new inference speed tier for its flagship GPT-5.6 Sol model that processes up to 750 tokens per second by running on Cerebras Systems' custom silicon. The mode delivers approximately 14 times the speed of standard GPT-5.6 Sol inference, which benchmarks at around 57 tokens per second according to independent measurements by Artificial Analysis.

The launch fulfills a commitment OpenAI made when it previewed the GPT-5.6 model family in June 2026, when it announced that Sol would be available on Cerebras hardware in July for select customers. The Ultrafast tier is now available through the OpenAI API alongside the existing standard and fast modes.

How Cerebras Makes It Possible

Traditional GPU inference faces a fundamental bottleneck: model weights live in external DRAM and must be streamed into compute units for every token generated. For single-turn queries, this latency is manageable. For agentic workflows — where models make dozens of sequential reasoning steps, tool calls, and coordination passes — the delays compound rapidly.

https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2087947721936359705

Cerebras eliminates this constraint through its Wafer-Scale Engine (WSE-3), fabricated from an entire silicon wafer rather than individual chips. The architecture provides 44 gigabytes of on-chip SRAM with 21 petabytes per second of memory bandwidth, compared to the Nvidia H100's bandwidth, which Cerebras says is approximately 7,000 times lower. Model weights stay on-chip permanently, so every token pulls from local memory rather than external storage.

"A 100,000-token agentic reasoning chain that takes approximately 2,000 seconds at 50 tokens per second takes roughly 133 seconds at 750 tokens per second, collapsing what would otherwise be a multi-hour background job into something that fits inside an interactive workflow."

— TechTimes

Pricing and Positioning

Ultrafast mode carries a premium over standard GPT-5.6 Sol pricing. Standard Sol costs $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens. The Ultrafast tier is priced at $12.50 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens — a 2.5x markup that reflects the specialized hardware costs.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=6SeqJTdc9M4

The pricing positions Ultrafast for specific use cases where latency directly blocks adoption: real-time coding agents, interactive reasoning chains, and automated pipelines where each second of delay cascades across dozens of sequential calls. Enterprise teams running high-volume agentic workloads will need to weigh the speed gains against the cost increase.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family also includes Terra ($2.50/$15 per million tokens) and Luna ($1/$6), offering developers a clear trade-off matrix across intelligence, speed, and cost.

The Competitive Landscape

The Cerebras partnership represents a strategic diversification for OpenAI, which has historically relied almost entirely on Nvidia GPUs for inference. The move comes as competition in the AI infrastructure space intensifies, with Google deploying custom TPUs, Amazon investing in Trainium chips, and a growing ecosystem of AI-specific silicon startups.

OpenAI's earlier collaboration with Cerebras produced GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark in February 2026, a smaller model that achieved over 1,000 tokens per second. Ultrafast extends this approach to a frontier-class model, though it uses weight streaming from external memory rather than the pure on-chip mode that powered Spark.

The speed advantage is substantial compared to competitors. Anthropic's Claude Opus runs at roughly 56 tokens per second, making GPT-5.6 Sol on Cerebras approximately 13 times faster at raw output generation.

What's Next

Access to Ultrafast mode is initially limited to select API customers as Cerebras scales capacity. OpenAI has not announced when broader availability will follow or whether the mode will extend to ChatGPT consumer products. For enterprise developers building latency-sensitive AI applications, the message is clear: frontier-model intelligence no longer requires frontier-model wait times.
